content.overview: Section 41 provides that a company may, after passing a special resolution in its general meeting, issue depository receipts in any foreign country in such manner, and subject to such conditions, as may be prescribed.
content.glance: Special resolution in general meeting; issue of depository receipts in any foreign country; manner and conditions as prescribed.
content.study: A company may issue depository receipts in any foreign country only after passing a special resolution in its general meeting, and only in the manner and subject to the conditions prescribed under the Act and rules (including the Companies (Issue of Global Depository Receipts) Rules, 2014). Section 41 is the statutory gateway for GDRs; the detailed operational conditions sit in the prescribed rules and applicable regulatory frameworks. Current-law framing: confirm special resolution; confirm foreign depository-receipt issue; apply the prescribed manner and conditions.

sections.heading: Special resolution
sections.body: The company must pass a special resolution in its general meeting before issuing depository receipts.

sections.heading: Foreign issue
sections.body: Depository receipts may be issued in any foreign country.

sections.heading: Prescribed manner and conditions
sections.body: Issue must be in such manner, and subject to such conditions, as may be prescribed under the Act and the applicable rules.

examples.title: GDR after special resolution
examples.body: A company passes a special resolution in general meeting and issues depository receipts in a foreign market in the prescribed manner and subject to the prescribed conditions.

hypotheticals.question: Can the Board alone authorise a GDR issue?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 41 requires a special resolution in the general meeting. Board action alone is insufficient.

distinctions.title: GDR (s. 41) vs private placement (s. 42)
distinctions.left: Foreign depository receipts after special resolution
distinctions.right: Domestic private placement to identified persons under numerical cap

misconceptions.correction: Section 41 requires a special resolution in the general meeting.

misconceptions.trap: Section 41 itself contains all operational conditions for GDRs.
misconceptions.correction: The section is enabling; manner and conditions are as prescribed (rules and applicable frameworks).

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should Section 41 be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm special resolution in general meeting. II. Identify proposed foreign depository-receipt issue. III. Apply the prescribed manner and conditions. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Facts; statutory ingredients of s. 41 (special resolution; foreign issue; prescribed conditions); precise compliance or relief finding.

examTips: State the exact enabling text: special resolution + foreign country + prescribed manner/conditions.
Emphasise that detailed conditions live in the prescribed rules, not in the section itself.
